title: Pomerania
capsule: The Duchy of Pomerania emerged as a coherent Slavic polity under the Griffin dynasty after Christianisation campaigns by Otto of Bamberg in 1124–1128, with Duke Wartislaw I consolidating ducal authority over the Oder and Baltic coastal territories. The attestation window of 1139–1188 covers the reigns of Wartislaw I and his successors as Pomerania navigated competing overlordships of the Holy Roman Empire, Denmark, and Poland; Bogislaw I secured recognition from Emperor Frederick Barbarossa at the Diet of Merseburg in 1181, formalising imperial feudal status. Denmark asserted overlordship from 1185, limiting Griffin autonomy until a later recovery of independence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's core territory along the Oder and Pomeranian coast is well attested in German and Polish sources; internal sub-divisions and peripheral boundaries in this period are less precisely documented.
